record.context_brief: Rossi problem for complete intersection semigroups
record.original_question: Let Gamma be a complete intersection numerical semigroup, let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]], let m be the maximal ideal of R_Gamma, let G_Gamma = gr(R_Gamma), and let HF_{G_Gamma}(j) = dim_k(m^j/m^{j+1}) be the Hilbert function of the associated graded ring. Is this Hilbert function always non-decreasing as j increases?

evidence.quote: The Hilbert function of GΓ = gr(RΓ ) is the numerical function HFGΓ : N → N defined as HFGΓ (j) = dimk[mj/mj+1]. Problem 28 (Rossi’s Problem [R11, Problem 4.9]). Let Γ be a complete intersection numerical semigroup. Is the Hilbert function HFGΓ non-decreasing?

artifact.category_tag: Hilbert functions of numerical semigroup rings
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field. A numerical semigroup is a subset $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. Given a minimal generating set $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots < n_e$ of $\Gamma$, the associated semigroup ring is
$$R_\Gamma := k[[\Gamma]] = k[[t^{n_1}, t^{n_2}, \ldots, t^{n_e}]] \subseteq k[[t]],$$
which is a one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m} = (t^{n_1}, \ldots, t^{n_e})$. The numerical semigroup $\Gamma$ is called a complete intersection if the defining ideal of $R_\Gamma$ in the polynomial presentation $k[[x_1, \ldots, x_e]] 	woheadrightarrow R_\Gamma$ (with $x_i \mapsto t^{n_i}$) is generated by exactly $e-1$ elements; equivalently, $R_\Gamma$ is a complete intersection ring.

Let
$$G_\Gamma := \mathrm{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(R_\Gamma) =  igoplus_{j \ge 0} \mathfrak{m}^j / \mathfrak{m}^{j+1}$$
denote the associated graded ring of $R_\Gamma$ with respect to $\mathfrak{m}$. Define the Hilbert function of $G_\Gamma$ by
$$\mathrm{HF}_{G_\Gamma}(j) := \dim_k  igl( \mathfrak{m}^j / \mathfrak{m}^{j+1}  igr), \qquad j \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every complete intersection numerical semigroup $\Gamma$, the Hilbert function $\mathrm{HF}_{G_\Gamma}$ is non-decreasing, i.e.
$$\mathrm{HF}_{G_\Gamma}(j) \le \mathrm{HF}_{G_\Gamma}(j+1) \qquad 	ext{for all } j \ge 0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The general Rossi conjecture (for one-dimensional Gorenstein local rings) was disproved by Oneto–Strazzanti–Tamone (arXiv:1602.00334), who constructed Gorenstein numerical semigroup rings with strictly decreasing Hilbert function. However, their counterexamples are not complete intersections, and the complete-intersection case of Rossi's question remains open. It has been verified for several subfamilies (e.g., complete intersections obtained by gluing, certain 4-generated cases, and specific symmetric/pseudo-symmetric monomial curves), but no general proof or counterexample for arbitrary complete intersection numerical semigroups appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: One-dimensional Gorenstein local rings with decreasing Hilbert function
status_evidence.snippet: Oneto, Strazzanti, Tamone construct infinitely many one-dimensional Gorenstein local rings whose Hilbert function decreases, giving counterexamples to Rossi's question in the Gorenstein case (but not in the complete intersection case).
status_evidence.claim: The general Rossi conjecture is false for Gorenstein rings, but the constructed counterexamples are not complete intersections.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert functions of Gorenstein monomial curves (Arslan–Mete)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides families of complete intersection numerical semigroups with non-decreasing Hilbert function, supporting Rossi's question in the complete intersection case.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results exist for complete intersection numerical semigroups.

status_evidence.title: Gluing and Hilbert functions of monomial curves
status_evidence.snippet: Uses gluing of numerical semigroups to produce families of complete intersection local rings with non-decreasing Hilbert functions, supporting Rossi's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Rossi's question is verified for large families of complete intersections obtained by gluing.
